literal: Desirelessness like excellent wealth here is not; there also to that equal is not.
translation: There is no excellent wealth in this world like desirelessness, and there is nothing equal to it anywhere else.
modern: ஆசையின்மைக்கு ஒப்பான சிறந்த செல்வம் இவ்வுலகில் வேறு இல்லை; அவ்வுலகிலும் அதற்கு இணையானது எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: The couplet declares that the absence of desire is the greatest possible wealth. It uses the word 'ஈண்டு' (here) to refer to the present world and 'ஆண்டும்' (there) to refer to any other realm or future state. By comparing desirelessness to 'விழுச்செல்வம்' (excellent wealth), it shows that true richness comes from not wanting things, rather than accumulating them. Thus, freedom from craving is presented as an unmatched treasure in any existence.
